beginner.whatItIs: The progress track that fills when you kill people with infantry weapons. There is no class to select - shooting someone is what feeds it.
beginner.whyItMatters: It pays the most per action of any track, and it is the only one where the thing that earns it also loses you your kit when it goes wrong.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Lean on it when you can afford to die. If you cannot, one of the tracks that pays for helping is a cheaper route to the same overall level.

beginner.whatItIs: The progress track that fills when you heal and revive teammates.
beginner.whyItMatters: A basic heal only needs someone injured, not someone down, which makes it the most repeatable source of progress in the game and one you can earn without entering a gunfight.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Level it when you are new and broke. It earns while your kit stays on your back, which is the opposite of how the combat track works.

beginner.whatItIs: The progress track fed by building, hauling supplies and repairing. Every hammer swing on a structure, every supply crate you buy for the team and every vehicle you patch up feeds this one.
beginner.whyItMatters: Building pays you three separate times rather than once at the end: a trickle per hammer hit, a bump at each marked point, and a lump when the structure finishes. Buying a supply crate or resupplying a teammate pays a flat amount each time. None of it needs you to win a gunfight.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Level it when you want unlocks without risking your kit, and when you want the belt-fed guns: the M500 opens at 10, the M249 SAW at 15 and the PKM at 30, and no other track will give you them.

name: Recon
summary: XP Class - Spotting for the team.

beginner.whatItIs: The progress track fed by marking enemies for other people. You get the credit when a teammate kills something you pointed out, which the game calls a Spot Assist.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is the one track that pays you for a fight you did not take, and it is also the one nobody has measured. The source has not confirmed what a spot is worth in XP or cash, so this is the single class you cannot rank against the other five.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Run it when you are already sitting somewhere with a view and a squad out in front of you. It gates the long guns - the SV98 at 19, the MK22 at 25, the BMR-308 at 30 and the AMR 50 at 35 - so feed it if you want a rifle that reaches.

beginner.whatItIs: The progress track for ground vehicles. Ferrying teammates toward the fighting feeds it, and so does anything you kill while you are still sitting in the vehicle.
beginner.whyItMatters: Dropping a teammate at the contested area pays once on arrival and again if they are still alive a few seconds later, so one trip can pay you twice. Kills made from inside a ground vehicle are credited here rather than to your fighting track, which is why the tank is the quickest way up this one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Take it when the team needs bodies moved and you would rather drive than walk. The truck opens at level 4, so it is cheap to start; the tank sits at 35 and is a long way off.

beginner.whatItIs: The progress track for helicopters. Flying supplies into the contested area is what feeds it.
beginner.whyItMatters: Setting one supply pallet down in the zone is worth more XP than any other single confirmed action in the game - roughly nine times what patching up a teammate pays. A smaller crate pays less but still well, and carrying people pays what driving them does.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Fly it when you want the fastest climb available to somebody who is not shooting anyone, and you can live with a slow start: the first helicopter does not open until level 10.
